note: The expected result for every source, written before any extraction or binding code existed, so a score against this file does not reflect rules tuned to it. Text fields are checked by the listed phrases, not by exact wording. A claim key (A, B, K1, K2, C) is a name used only in this file.

A.summary: After an SFP replacement on older units, the interface can be UP with normal optics and zero traffic. Check the counters; if they stay at zero, disable and enable the interface before replacing hardware or rebooting.

estimates.note: Kept as the engineer's estimate with its source. It does not become an age limit.

scope_refined_by.note: The teller names a firmware version, so the scope becomes confirmed from this source onwards. Before it the scope is undefined, and any reach to another unit is named a guess.

B.summary: On these old units, replace the SFP first: the cage is usually the bad part, and a bounce hides the fault for a while.
B.corrected_after_first_run: Corrected on 6.11.2026 after the first scored run, by the owner's decision (docs/DECISIONS.md row 4). This file first bound the claim to TRN-051. The model left it waiting: the advice is about old units in general, the expert observed nothing on TRN-051, and that unit only prompted the comment. A correction made after seeing a result is weaker evidence than the rest of this file.

K1.summary: The key to the barrier on the Nilo private road is in the grey box under the mailbox at the junction.

K2.summary: The barrier key is now in the maintenance hut by the junction, on the hook inside the door.

C.summary: On TRN-100 the traffic loss after the SFP swap was a VLAN missing from the service profile on xe-0/1/0.
C.note: A one-off finding on one port. Extracting it is neither required nor penalised.

K3.summary: The key to the Koski gate was moved last week to the control room's key cabinet, slot 7, when the old lock box was replaced. Told in Finnish; the words stay Finnish.
K3.written_after_the_first_rows: Added on 7.11.2026 evening, before its source was read by the model, for the second cut's new sources.
K3.note: "Viime viikolla" is kept as words and not turned into a date: the code resolves only the phrases it knows, and an unknown time stays unknown.

sources.note: The same teller as the Teams conversation, so one claim with two sources and one told row. The email has no time; that does not stop the binding. Its sentence about several cases stays readable through the source link, but it is the teller's own general statement and not an event, so it never reaches the rendered evidence.
A complaint about old units is not a claim.
It names TRN-042 and firmware, but only about a schedule. It must not trigger a recheck, and it is not the firmware event.
Yesterday is resolved by code from the message's own date, not by the model.
The on-call relays the expert's advice, which is not a new telling. The thread also names TRN-042, but the outcome belongs to TRN-051.
Traffic comes back at the end, but the thread says it was the VLAN. A failure on another generation is not a dispute.

must_not: a new told row on claim A
sources.note: Neither expert reports an event here, and repeating an opinion is not a new telling. Both claims stay visible and the agent does not choose.
A Finnish thread. The site is named in inflected forms, which the graph holds as aliases; the claim text stays in the speaker's Finnish.

A ticket's worklog, a third kind of source, read by the same reader. The on-call's check of the service profile is the advice already known from the chat (C); the ticket adds its outcome, and the relayed bounce advice its failure on TRN-100.
sources.corrected_after_first_run: Corrected on 7.11.2026 evening after the first scored run, marked here as the measurement rules require. The row first named C as the ticket's claim; the scorer cannot address C, because C is optional on the thread it comes from and gets no id. The ticket's first entry relays the chat's bounce advice (A) and reports that it did not help on TRN-100, which the model read as a failure outcome on A, and its second entry reports the service profile fix, which the model tied to C with a success outcome. This row now checks A and leaves C optional, so the success on C is in the recorded answer but not scored.

variants.note: Without a date, yesterday stays unresolved, even though received_at is known: that is information time, not world time.

telemetry_outcomes.note: Counters stay at zero after admin_up. They rise only after ev-405, a configuration change, and that rise is not an outcome of the bounce.

clock.note: The demo clock decides which sources and events are known. Acceptance cases that need different states of knowledge run at different clock values.
